thesis: Affirm's confirmed FQ4 2026 disclosure showed GMV growth of 36%, revenue growth of 33%, RLTC growth of 39%, and a 13% GAAP operating margin, with fiscal 2027 guidance for more than $64 billion of GMV and more than a 14.5% GAAP operating margin; this suggests the growth and profitability inflection is operating-led. The strongest counter-evidence is that $1.6 billion of GAAP net income was boosted by a deferred-tax valuation-allowance release and fiscal 2026 credit-loss provisions rose 29%, but that does not change the long read because RLTC growth and GAAP operating margin exclude the tax benefit and improved despite the higher credit costs.
invalidation: GMV and revenue growth decelerate materially while credit-loss provisions grow faster than revenue, or the company withdraws its fiscal 2027 GAAP operating-margin outlook.

thesis: The current volume signal follows S&P Dow Jones Indices' confirmed addition of Tenable to the S&P SmallCap 600 before the August 31 open, so the setup is primarily mechanical index demand rather than fresh operating evidence. Tenable's confirmed Q2 results are credible counter-evidence—revenue grew 8.6%, GAAP operating income turned positive, and the company raised its non-GAAP full-year outlook—but those July results predate the signal and do not make one-time benchmark-tracking demand a repeatable fundamental catalyst, so the shares are avoided this run.
invalidation: After the index rebalance passes, a fresh company disclosure shows sustained organic customer and revenue acceleration rather than volume driven mainly by benchmark-tracking demand.
sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices index-addition release: https://press.spglobal.com/2026-08-26-Tenable-Holdings-Set-to-Join-S-P-SmallCap-600

thesis: KE Holdings' confirmed unaudited Q2 2026 results showed GTV growth of 6.3% and GAAP net-income growth of 100.8%, while net revenue fell 5.7%, mobile MAU declined, and active-agent count contracted as lower operating expense reflected cost optimization. The transaction growth and margin expansion support a constructive long read, but the offsetting top-line and user-footprint contraction leaves the durability of the cost-led earnings improvement unresolved, keeping conviction low.
invalidation: GTV turns negative or revenue contraction persists while the gross-margin and GAAP net-income improvement fades.

thesis: Rubrik's confirmed Q2 fiscal 2027 results showed subscription ARR growth of 33%, revenue growth of 38%, positive operating and free cash flow, and raised non-GAAP full-year guidance; this suggests demand and operating leverage remain constructive. The strongest counter-evidence is Rubrik's disclosed DOJ matter: a former sales employee was indicted in October 2024 and the company found employee communications tied to potential federal-law violations involving government contracts; current growth does not erase that qualifying governance history, so the long read remains low-conviction.
invalidation: Subscription ARR or revenue growth slows materially, full-year guidance is reduced, operating cash flow turns negative, or the DOJ matter expands into charges or sanctions against Rubrik.

thesis: Reports that Advent International and Stripe ended their PayPal pursuit removed the takeover premium and explain the high-volume selloff, but PayPal did not confirm the report, making the current catalyst sentiment-driven and mechanical rather than a company-disclosed fundamental deterioration. PayPal's confirmed Q2 progress and raised non-GAAP full-year guidance are positive counter-evidence, but those older operating results do not restore the abandoned deal support, so the shares are avoided this run at low conviction.
invalidation: PayPal or the bidders confirm a renewed transaction process, or a fresh company disclosure shows organic execution strong enough to replace the lost takeover catalyst.
sources: Axios on the ended PayPal pursuit: https://www.axios.com/2026/08/28/stripe-advent-end-paypal-pursuit
